title: Fix the forgetting chat
scenario: You have been working in one long chat for hours. You ask about a preference you stated near the beginning, and the answer is confidently wrong — the start of the conversation has fallen out of the context window.
task: What is the best next step?

options.text: Repeat “please remember everything I said” and ask again.
options.feedback: Wishing does not widen the window. The dropped text is gone — an instruction cannot bring it back.

options.text: Ask for a summary of the decisions so far, then start a fresh chat with that summary and your question.
options.feedback: Yes — carry forward a compact summary into a clean window. This beats a long chat with missing context in almost every case.

options.text: Say the preference again as a single line and continue in the same chat.
options.feedback: Better than nothing — but the long chat is still crowded, and the next hundred messages may push your line out again. A clean window with a compact brief is more reliable.

options.text: Nothing — models eventually remember everything from the session.
options.feedback: There is no store behind the window. If it is not in the current context, it is not available.

hints: What is the smallest, most relevant context you could bring to a clean window?
explanation: The window is finite working memory, and the oldest content falls out first. The durable fix is a carry-forward habit: summarize the essentials, start fresh, paste the brief. Restating a line helps briefly; managing the window deliberately helps permanently.
